title: Feasts, sacred houses, gifts, oaths, vows, and prayers for grace are as divine as sacrifice
source_text: XXIV. Caeterum ad actus & signa cultus Deo proprii, Theologi Reformati plurima pertinere putant, non minus quam sacrificia. Qualia sunt, secundum eorum sententiam, dies festi, aedes sacrae, & donaria in aedibus sacris dicata & appensa, juramenta, vota, & preces, quibus bona corporis & animae, ac praesertim dona gratiae & gloriae, ab aliquo poscimus. Proinde quemadmodum, Scholae Romanae judicio, Latriam creaturae deferre censeretur, qui sub quocunque praetextu illi sacrificaret, nec excusaretur dicendo, se creaturae cuipiam sacrificium offerre, non absolute, sed relative, nec tanquam Deo ipsi, sed tanquam amico cuidam & ministro ipsius Dei, ad quem tandem honor ille sacrificii, ex ejus intentione, sit ultimo referendus: sic quoque, juxta Reformatos, a crimine divini cultus creaturis oblati non purgatur ille qui creaturis ullis aedes sacras dicat, donaria offert, illis vota facit, & per eas jurat, ab iisque petit gratiam & gloriam, quantumlibet profiteatur se illa creaturis praestare atque exhibere, aliter quam ipsi Deo, & sic ut velit ista ad Dei cultum & gloriam referre.
pass_a_gloss: But the Reformed theologians think that very many things belong to the acts and signs of the cult proper to God, no less than sacrifices. Such, according to their opinion, are feast days, sacred buildings, and gifts dedicated and hung up in sacred buildings, oaths, vows, and prayers by which we ask someone for goods of body and soul, and especially the gifts of grace and glory. Hence, just as, in the judgment of the Roman School, a man would be held to pay Latria to a creature who sacrificed to it under any pretext, and would not be excused by saying that he offers sacrifice to some creature not absolutely but relatively, and not as to God himself but as to some friend and minister of God himself, to whom that honor of the sacrifice is finally to be referred according to his intention: so also, according to the Reformed, a man is not cleared of the crime of divine cult offered to creatures who dedicates sacred buildings to any creatures, offers gifts, makes vows to them, swears by them, and asks grace and glory from them, however much he professes that he renders and shows those things to creatures otherwise than to God himself, and so as to will that they be referred to the cult and glory of God.
pass_b_english: Feasts, sacred buildings, dedicated gifts, oaths, vows, and prayers for bodily goods and especially for grace and glory count, for the Reformed, as signs of God's own cult, no less than sacrifice.
Rome itself would not excuse sacrifice to a creature by calling it relative, or offered to God's friend so as to be referred at last to God.
The same plea does not excuse dedicating churches, offering gifts, vowing, swearing, or asking grace and glory of a creature.

choices.why: Church-dedication is listed with sacrifice as divine cult, not as a neutral memorial.
